observation.visible_scene: An outdoor winter scene on a snow-dusted concrete step/porch. A blue plastic bowl sits on the step, partly filled with dark liquid, with a black-and-silver digital thermometer resting across its rim (probe in the liquid, display handle out to the right). Loose snow piles line the edges of the step, and a beige door/wall and white trim are visible at the top of the frame.
visible_changes: The bowl and thermometer remain in the same position throughout; no object translation or rotation is observed.

Around frame 3 the doorway area at the top briefly shows an opened/gapped view (a dark opening with a light edge) before the frame returns to its earlier appearance; this is a small, transient background change.

From roughly frame 12 onward, light-colored mottled/swirled patches appear on the liquid surface inside the bowl, growing and spreading across the lower portion of the liquid and persisting to the end of the clip (a surface texture change rather than a change in the bowl's contents' volume).
Throughout, there is only slight handheld camera jitter; the overall framing of the bowl, snow, and door stays essentially fixed.
outside_clip_unknowns: The cause of the light surface texture forming in the liquid (e.g., freezing, added material, or reflection) is not shown.
Whether the brief door-area change at frame 3 corresponds to any action or is incidental is not visible.
The reading on the thermometer display and any outcome after the clip are not determinable.
uncertain_details: Whether the frame-3 top-of-image change is a door opening, a camera shift, or a transient reflection is ambiguous.
The white/swirled pattern in the liquid could be ice crystals, foam, or a reflection; its exact nature is not confirmable from these frames alone.
